newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Health buys home health care firm.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Health buys home health care firm.

text.p: Integrated Health Services Inc said Thursday it has acquired First American Health Care of Georgia Inc for $154.1 million in cash.

Under the deal, First American will be merged into a wholly owned subsidiary of Integrated Health. Aside from the $154.1 million that was paid at the closing, the deal carries a contingent earnout of up to an additional $159 million payable in years 2000 through 2004, it said.
The company said First American is the largest privately held provider of home health care in the United States, with more than 400 agencies in 21 states.
After the transaction, Integrated Health said it will be the fourth largest provider of home health services with about 600 agencies in 24 states.

First American had filed for protection under Chapter 11 in bankruptcy court because of the suspension of Medicare payments. The payments were suspended due to a dispute between First American and the federal government involving cost disallowances and reimbursement liabilities.
Payments were resumed in February under orders from the bankruptcy court, the company said.

A settlement agreement has been signed allowing First American to pay $255 million to the federal government and stipulating that Integrated Health will have no liability for activities occurring prior to the acquisition.
The settlement agreement and the acquisition have been approved by the bankruptcy court.
